content.text: I read every input file and every section of the draft, then built a limitation-by-limitation ledger against the disclosure and the affirmative USER turns.

input.summary:
Full ledger built and traced. Authority used: input/disclosure.md plus the single technical USER turn in input/conversation.md ("...I want to also add autonomous mode... we don't even need to pull or move it with the hand, we can add small stirring elements and let the vibrations cause a constant forward motion"); input/brief.md was used only for title, applicant/inventor, the "Not applicable." cross-reference and government-support entries. All other USER turns are operational resume/repair instructions and were treated as non-disclosure; all YOU turns were treated as context only.

CLAIMS: every limitation of independent claims 1 (device), 11 (system) and 16 (method) and of dependent claims 2-10, 12-15 and 17-20 was traced. Rigid base with first/second side, motor coupled to the first side, air-extraction mechanism (vacuum pump) coupled to the first side and in fluid communication with a chamber on the second side, rigid low-friction loop/skirt at the perimeter of the second side (plastic, metal, PTFE, combinations of rigid materials), non-sealing behaviour, air entering beneath the perimeter through a clearance, extraction rate sufficient to hold the chamber below atmosphere while air keeps entering, the resulting pressure differential holding the device down without operator force, an all-rigid motor-to-tile path free of rubber/foam giving substantially less damping, free sliding to successive areas while the vacuum continuously maintains contact, guiding handles, and the rope/wire/cable pulling element with decoupled position-versus-hold control all rest on exact affirmative disclosure sentences. Claim 10 ("one or more stirring elements carried by the vibration device") rests on the autonomous-mode USER turn. No claim limitation was left untraced, and claims and description use the same terms and relationships throughout (perimeter member, bearing face as end face, clearance, vibration transmission path, pressure differential).

NUMERALS: the ledger 10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 34, 36, 38, 40, 42, 44, 46, 48 was checked against every use in the description and in all six briefs. Each numeral denotes one part everywhere it appears, each table entry appears on at least one sheet, and no brief introduces a numeral absent from the table or the description. The unused 28/30/32 gap leaves no orphan text. Numeral 10 means the whole machine consistently in FIGS. 1, 5 and 6, the single-body depiction in FIG. 6 being reconciled in the Brief Description.

FIGURES: all six briefs were compared with draft/07-drawings.md and with the description. Section-line designations are repeated identically in the resulting view, the source-view brief and the drawing description: "2-2" appears in the FIG. 2 brief view line, in the FIG. 3 brief (numeral 2 at both ends, leading to FIG. 2) and in the FIG. 2 drawing description; "4-4" appears in the FIG. 4 brief view line, in the FIG. 3 brief (numeral 4 at both ends, leading to FIG. 4) and in the FIG. 4 drawing description. The horizontal 2-2 cut yielding the two flush legs of FIG. 2 and the vertical 4-4 cut yielding the single fragmentary column of FIG. 4 are geometrically consistent with the ring of FIG. 3, and the bearing-at-2-2 / clearance-at-4-4 split matches the disclosed pair of facts (rigid contact maintained with the tile, air continuously entering beneath the rigid perimeter) while the application text stays position-neutral ("at a place along the perimeter member 24 at which the clearance 34 is present").

Depiction conventions were checked for leakage. The slab, band, ring, blocks, columns and stacked bands are generic outlines; the rectangular plan form, ring width, band depth, block order, section-line angular position, the port gap through the slab, the pulling-element attachment place and the number/place of the stirring elements are each disclaimed inside the brief that uses them. None of these conventions is verbalized in the title, field, background, summary, Brief Description, detailed description, claims or abstract: the application text never says "by way of example", never offers "any closed outline", never states a shape, width, count, proportion, taper, angle, runout, deeper end, circumferential position or contact topology for the bearing face, the clearance or the perimeter member, and never adds an optional embodiment to justify a drawn choice. The only figure-related statements in the application text are the standard "shown schematically", "omitted for clarity" and "shown enlarged for clarity" recitals, each matching its brief. The functional face (bearing face 26, drawn as a plain end line seen edge on), the clearance flow boundary and the fluid-communication opening are each an affirmatively disclosed functional part shown at minimum specificity.

TEXT: no drafting note, placeholder, bracketed to-do, open question, instruction to a person, unresolved alternative or internal comment remains in any of the ten draft sections. Background prior-art characterizations, including the [REF:...]-tagged passages, were not required to trace to the inventor and were not used to support any invention text; citation verification is left to the later independent review as instructed. Antecedent basis, the two-problem framing and its "second problem" antecedent, the Field/Summary/description/claims term set, and the abstract (under 150 words, no unsupported matter) are internally consistent. No unsupported technical assertion and no verified internal inconsistency was found.
